title: Delivering your pēpi
description:
There are several different ways of delivering your pēpi. The appropriate approach depends on your personal preferences, your health status and the medical necessities for your pregnancy.

Please be assured that choosing the delivery method is a shared decision making process between mum, their partner and whānau, and the trained healthcare providers (e.g. midwife, leading maternity carer (LMC), obstetrician). They will be present at your labour to support you as you give birth.

contentSections.title: Spontaneous
contentSections.content: Labour and muscle contractions begin naturally to open mum's cervix between weeks 37 and 40. The pēpi is delivered through the vagina without medical intervention or surgical tools. This is the standard approach for giving birth if there are no health concerns for mum or pēpi.

contentSections.title: Induced Labour
contentSections.content:
In this situation, labour and muscle contractions begin artificially for mum rather than naturally. The decision is made with the following in mind:
  • If your pēpi is overdue (e.g. 41 weeks)
  • Your waters are broken before labour starts
  • Mum or pēpi has a health problem, e.g. Gestational diabetes, Pre-eclampsia.

contentSections.title: C-Section
contentSections.content:
This is an operation where a cut is made through your abdomen and womb to deliver the pēpi. Mum is advised to take this option if vaginal birth is not possible or safe. There are many reasons for this, including:
  • The placenta is blocking the pēpi's path through the cervix;
  • Mum has had a previous C-section or a major surgery to the uterus;
  • The pēpi is premature or not developing well;
  • Both mum and pēpi have serious medical condition/complication.
